spark_scene.description: True-color satellite view of the main Hawaiian Islands from northwest to southeast over dark ocean with scattered white cumulus and cirrus clouds; the large southeastern island is partly cloud-covered with a faint translucent haze trailing south over the ocean.

plumes.label: pale blue-gray haze south of large island
plumes.visual_description: thin pale blue-gray translucent haze extending south-southwest from the southern tip of the large southeastern island over the dark ocean, distinct from the brighter white clouds over land

plumes.spark_label: pale blue-gray haze south of large island

firms.source: NASA GIBS FIRMS thermal anomaly layers (2026-10-17), rasterised
firms.note: counts are rendered marker pixels on a 0.005-deg grid, not individual detections
firms.volcanic_note: summit-caldera thermal detections (active vent glow), excluded from fire clusters

result.caveats: Big Island interior is partly cloud-covered so the over-land connection from summit to ocean haze is obscured; segmented upwind_end is ~90-110 km south of both summits and represents emergence from cloud, not true vent origin; Mauna Loa summit 10-m wind from 300 deg differs from Kilauea NE trades.
evidence: thin pale blue-gray translucent haze extending south-southwest from southern tip of Big Island over dark ocean, distinct from bright white textured cumulus/cirrus over land - matches vog, not cloud or brown smoke
volcanic_thermal_excluded kilauea-summit 316 indicates active summit vent glow at Kilauea, providing SO2 source for vog
nearest FIRMS clusters n=168 at 2.1 km and n=32 at 4.4 km from Kilauea summit are flank lava, not vegetation wildfire; only distant Honolulu fires 334.6 km away are unrelated
10-m wind at Kilauea summit from 030 deg at 16.7 km/h (NE trades) blows toward SSW, consistent with 179-km plume oriented SSW from island
plume geometry area 9122 km2 length 179 km centroid 18.718,-155.664 is downwind ocean vog accumulation despite upwind_end 89.7 km from Mauna Loa and 110.3 km from Kilauea due to cloud masking
pale blue-gray translucent faint haze, not bright white cloud and not brown smoke
active Kilauea vent with 316 excluded summit thermals plus 168+32 near-summit lava pixels supports Kilauea vog source
Kilauea NE wind 030/16.7 kmh drives SSW transport matching visual orientation; Honolulu fire source >330 km distant impossible

overall.rule: most hazardous class with confidence >= 0.70 (wildfire_smoke > vog_* > dust > cloud)
